description: By mapping past trends and forecasting future scenarios, our goal is to empower users to understand Earth's changing climate and explore sustainable solutions. Driven by science, animation, and technology, we aim to make Earth science engaging and impactful for everyone.
summary:
In a world increasingly dominated by industrialization, humanity—once an integral part of the ecosystem—has become a direct threat to its own planet. Yet, do we truly grasp this reality? Can the seemingly minor changes we make today trigger monumental consequences in the future?

Through Alternative Earth, we provide an integrated, interactive experience powered by authentic NASA data. Designed for the "Be an Earth System Trend Detective" challenge, our website allows you to explore the transformations occurring across Earth’s surface due to various climatic factors.

The platform forecasts environmental scenarios over the next 300 years and highlights specific wildlife species, illustrating their projected extinction rates based on your selected timeframe. Additionally, if you encounter any difficulties while navigating the site, ÉcoVie—your personal AI assistant—guides you through the different sections and answers your questions using verified data.

Based on your selected geographic region, the platform also reveals your individual role and offers actionable advice on how to save the planet.

After all, if we consider ourselves mere guests on this Earth, the least a courteous guest can do is leave the place just as they found it.
details:
roject Functionality & Architecture: The Alternative Earth is a zero-build-step web application utilizing HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript, hosted on GitHub Pages. It features an interactive 3D globe built with Three.js and a synchronized 2D map. Climate data is managed via a simplified emulator (js/model.js) anchored to IPCC AR6 projections and NASA datasets (GISTEMP, SRTM, EONET), allowing simulation across three SSP scenarios up to the year 2325. Python scripts (fetch_nasa_data.py) automate data refreshing.

Key Features & Tools:

  • ÉcoVie Assistant: A browser-based AI guide (js/guide.js, js/brain.js) providing contextual walkthroughs and querying integrated NASA datasets, technical reports, and Q&A databases.
  • Species Risk Model: Evaluates extinction probabilities for 28 climate-threatened species based on IUCN statuses and exposure to localized climate factors.
  • Localized Impact (“My Matter”): Correlates global warming scenarios with regional elevation and historical events to deliver location-specific sustainability advice.

Impact & Innovation: The project bridges abstract climate science and public awareness by gamifying 300-year environmental forecasting. By providing localized consequences and an interactive AI guide, it translates complex NASA and NOAA data into actionable personal responsibility to preserve planetary ecosystems.
